title: Finite-filtration and noetherian detection
his_statement: suite de composition finie; système de générateurs
statement: A family whose quotients finitely filter every object detects vanishing of right-exact functors and bounded-above cohomological functors; dual statement detects bounded-below contravariant functors. In a noetherian abelian category weak detection Hom(G,F)≠0 for some G whenever F≠0 gives the required finite filtration.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: The maximal-subobject argument and descending induction are valid. The displayed definition accidentally quantifies M∈C rather than M∈G; the proof uses G. Boundedness is essential for the induction.
fate: The bounded cohomological detection argument occurs in the published local-cohomology framework. The weak-generator terminology is fixed by the draft’s own definition; our finite-filtration proof makes its exact force explicit.

title: Support detects the zero functor
statement: For noetherian A and finite modules Mi supported on V(I), their union of supports equals V(I) iff Hom(Mi,F) jointly detects nonzero I-torsion modules. Finite I-torsion modules then have filtrations by quotients of Mi.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: Uses Ass Hom(M,F)=Supp(M)∩Ass(F), with M finite and F arbitrary. This is a weak detecting family, not the usual categorical generator whose Hom functor is faithful: over k[ε]/ε² the module k detects every nonzero finite module but cannot surject onto A.
fate: The support-based vanishing criterion is part of the published framework. The equality for associated primes and the weak-versus-faithful-generator distinction are checked separately.

title: Pointwise object extension needs descent
his_statement: à cause de l’unicité…la question est locale
statement: The draft asserts P3 relative to Y iff P3 at every x∈Y for a fibred category, and glues objects over W and U.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: False for arbitrary fibred categories. On the three-point spectral space with generic η and closed a,b, take U={η}; the discrete category has one object on each proper open and no object on X. Local punctured restrictions at a,b are equivalences, but global restriction is not essentially surjective. This is a prestack whose missing effective descent is exactly the gap. With a stack the noetherian induction works.
fate: The unrestricted fibred-category claim is refuted by a three-point prestack. Effective descent is the precise missing hypothesis; torsors and stacks supply it. No published source was found asserting the false unrestricted version.

title: Atoms of a trace and minimal projections
statement: The fragment relates atoms in a maximal abelian subalgebra to minimal projections, and sketches diffuse trace reduction.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: The ambient algebra b, trace faithfulness, and availability of characteristic projections are not defined on the supplied fragment. In a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal trace, an atomic projection of a MASA is minimal in the full algebra: a nontrivial corner projection would commute with the MASA and violate maximality. A point atom of a measure on a C*-spectrum alone need not give a continuous characteristic projection.
fate: The isolated fragment does not define enough of its ambient algebra to identify an unrestricted theorem. Published b is the uniform closure of the trace ideal; under faithful normal trace/von Neumann hypotheses the MASA atomic-projection implication is checked. This is a conditional reconstruction, not a decision about missing ink.

title: Weak convergence, norm convergence, and uniform convexity

This is distinct from uniform convexity: S1 is not strictly convex, and for p<1 the infinite-dimensional space is not locally convex. Fack–Kosaki5.2–5.3 gives the uniformly convex range1<p<infinity.

modern_statement: In a separated complete linearly topologized Q-algebra, exp and log are inverse on topologically nilpotent elements and1+such elements; natural under continuous algebra maps; preserve closed one-sided ideals in the indicated sense. modern_statement: Primitive base change is exact when Lambda is flat or the defining reduced-coproduct kernel sequence is pure. title: Nilpotent derivations and unipotent automorphisms
modern_statement: Over a Q-algebra, a globally nilpotent linear endomorphism D is a derivation of a bilinear product iff exp D preserves the product. For an augmented Lambda with I^N=0, Lambda-automorphisms of B reducing to identity correspond under log to Lambda-derivations into IB.
page_status: stated; polynomial argument implicit
present_check: exp(mD)=(exp D)^m for all integers m. If exp D preserves multiplication, the polynomial identity in m holds for infinitely many rational integers; comparing its linear coefficient proves the derivation law. Conversely the iterated Leibniz/binomial formula proves multiplicativity. Fixed vectors, commuting operators and invariant submodules are preserved because exp and log are polynomials.
literature_fate: The nilpotent logarithm/exponential correspondence over Q is established classical algebra. Adamus–Hajto2026 §2 explicitly states it and traces the converse to van den Essen2000 Proposition2.1.3; both the current article and the earlier book’s publisher record were opened. The manuscript’s nilpotent coefficient ideal makes the operators globally nilpotent, so the finite formulas apply. No characteristic-p extension or novelty claim is made.

title: Lê Dũng Tráng’s meromorphic denominator correction
modern_statement: Lê’s11Jan1968 letter corrects EGAIV20.1 and21: the denominator subsheaf consists of sections that remain non-zero-divisors on all open restrictions. title: Gluing unramified sections across a dense open and thickening
modern_statement: For unramified X→Y, a schematically dense open U⊂Y and closed Y0⊂Y with the same underlying space, compatible sections on U andY0 are asserted to glue uniquely.
page_status: stated without proof
present_check: Uniqueness follows from the open diagonal plus schematic density in the appropriate separated/local argument. Existence is subtler: unramified is not formally smooth. A blanket appeal to nilpotent invariance of étale sites would not establish this statement for arbitrary unramified X.
literature_fate: Stacks00US supplies the unramified algebraic framework; Rydh concerns effective descent of étale morphisms under specific subtrusiveness hypotheses. Their role is explicitly a comparison framework.

title: Nonnoetherian regular sequences and the Koszul replacement
modern_statement: Outside the noetherian case, regular sequences need not be permutable. The proposed replacement uses vanishing of positive Koszul homology, gives a quasiregular ideal, is independent of minimal generators, descends fpqc, and composes for immersions. In the noetherian case the notions agree.
page_status: proof claims partly checked by Berthelot; editorial plan to correct EGA

title: A-modules versus B-modules in adic separation
his_words: tout quotient de tout sous-module de M
modern_statement: Deligne rejects the assertion that all A-subquotients of a finite B-module are J-adically separated when A,B are noetherian and JB⊂radB. It is valid for finite B-subquotients, not arbitrary A-subquotients. The graded example also fails for nongraded quotients.
page_status: counterexamples in letter; earlier objection reinstated15Dec1966

title: Algebraic solution sets are not linearly compact affine spaces
modern_statement: Deligne identifies an error in EGAIV0.19.3.12: sets of algebra homomorphism lifts across a non-square-zero ideal need not be affine linear spaces. Infinite systems of polynomial conditions over an infinite field can have all finite subsystems solvable and no global solution.
page_status: counterexample and proof criticism
present_check: For an infinite fieldk, equations(x_infty−u)y_u=1 for everyu∈k have each finite subsystem solvable by choosing x_infty outside the finite forbidden set; no full solution exists because x_infty itself equals someu. Primary EGAIV1 printed85–86 visibly calls the lift set a closed linear variety. This invalidates that proof, not automatically the theorem.
literature_fate: Exact published withdrawal: EGA IV4, Liste 3 de corrections, IV no.8, printed p.347 (1967), expressly suppresses 0.19.3.12 because its sets W_lambda, U_lambda and V_lambda are not linear varieties. This matches Deligne’s 17 October 1966 criticism. The finite-solvability example checks the invalid proof method; it is not represented as a counterexample to every hypothesis of the withdrawn proposition.

title: Relative finite Tor dimension and Tor/pro-completion
modern_statement: For local noetherian A→B, finite A-moduleN, finite B-moduleM and idealm⊂A, the pro-systems Tor_p^A(N/m^kN,M) and Tor_p^A(N,M)/m^k are asserted isomorphic. Deligne uses this toward the relative depth formula with finite Tor dimension and revisits the proof at the letter’s end.
page_status: proof sketched using flat cover; author flags awkwardness and cannot give the simpler direct proof
present_check: After faithfully flat completion of B, use a flat noetherian local A-algebra C surjecting onto completedB. Both N tensor_A C and completedM are finite C-modules. Resolve completedM by finite free C-modules; Artin–Rees makes pro-I-adic completion exact on the resulting complex of finite C-modules, so pro-homology equals the completion pro-system of homology. Flat base change identifies this with the stated A-Tor. Faithful flatness of B→Bhat reflects the pro-zero kernels and cokernels. The argument is supplied in proof_notes.md and is stronger than equality of inverse limits.
literature_fate: The Artin–Rees pro-Tor mechanism is explicitly proved in Stacks15.28.3 (0911), citing Quillen’s Lemma9.9; modern Cohen factorization supplies the flat noetherian cover. The relative two-module statement is independently reconstructed here from those exact ingredients; it is not claimed to be literally the statement of0911.

title: Deligne’s minimal Cohen factorization
his_words: C plat sur A; C0 régulier ... degrés0 et1
modern_statement: For local noetherian A→B withB complete, seek A→C→B withC complete local noetherian, C→B surjective, C flat overA, regular closed fibre, and induced graded fibre map bijective in degrees0 and1. title: Further Deligne errata and suggested simplifications
his_words: homomorphisme local ... signe ... K′=K tensor Ahat faux
modern_statement: The letter proposes: drop a noetherian hypothesis in0.16.1.9 by Bourbaki integrality; weaken formal-projectivity assumptions in0.19.4.6; use semi-exactness of Exalcotop in0.19.4.7; insert local in0.19.8.3; reverse the chosen dx sign in0.20.4.6; remove integral-closure hypothesis in0.20.4.13(iv); and rejects EGAIII4.3.6 K′=K⊗A Ahat generally.
page_status: errata and unproved simplification suggestions, with question mark
present_check: Three exact checks are now complete. Printed0.16.1.9 p24 assumes noetherianity; its dimension equality extends without it because the faithful finite-module determinant trick makes B/Ann_B(M) integral over A/Ann_A(M), and integral extensions preserve dimension. Printed0.19.8.3 pp110–111 claims uniqueness among homomorphisms from a prime local ring: locality is essential, since every Z_(p) maps nonlocally to Q. Printed0.20.4.13(iv) p127 has the integral-closure hypothesis; localization gives Omega_B/A tensor Frac(B)=Omega_Frac(B)/Frac(A)=0 for an algebraic separable fraction extension, without integral closure. The0.20.4.6 sign is a convention requiring coherent propagation. The19.4.6–7 simplification proposals are not independently certified. Original EGAIII1,4.3.6 printedp133, has the alleged false equality. For A=Q[x,y]_(x,y), the prime (y−(exp(x)−1)) in Ahat contracts to0 and survives localization by A minus0, so Frac(A) tensor_A Ahat is not a field. The desired analytically-integral implies unibranch argument nevertheless works with the natural inclusion into Frac(Ahat). Full details are in proof_notes.md §11. The later published errata confirm the first three corrections and record the sign change, subject to the printed old/new-label transposition just described.
literature_fate: Exact later errata: EGA IV4 Liste 3 de corrections, IV nos.6,9,12–14, printed pp.347–348 (1967). No.6 removes noetherianity from 0.16.1.9; no.9 inserts local in 0.19.8.3/4; nos.12–13 change the differential convention; no.14 removes integral closure in 0.20.4.13(iv) and supplies a denominator-clearing argument. The first p1/p2 instruction in no.12 itself has old/new labels reversed relative to the original p.125; its explicit tensor formula and no.13 determine the intended change. The 19.4.6–7 suggested proof simplifications remain separate bounded verification questions. The III4.3.6 equality is now verified false in the original print, while its conclusion is independently recovered using the natural injection.

title: Deligne’s deferred proof request for the théorème de Lefschetz vache
author: Pierre Deligne; letter to A.Grothendieck dated17October1966
his_words: Je n'ai pas l'intention d'essayer de démontrer, cette année, le ``théorème de \unsure{Lefschetz|Lefchetz} vache''. J'espère donc que tu trouves quelqu'un qui le fasse.

statement: The historical sentence requests a proof of the named theorem without specifying a base field, coefficients or smoothness/projectivity hypotheses. The exact terminology in SGA7 XVIII5.2.2 identifies the standard hard-Lefschetz interpretation: for X smooth projective of pure dimension n over an algebraically closed field k, an ample invertible sheaf L, and a prime l different from char(k), cup product with c1(L)^i gives an isomorphism H^(n-i)(X,Q_l) -> H^(n+i)(X,Q_l(i)) for every i>=0. This precise statement is the later matched theorem, not a transcription of hypotheses from the letter.

statement: Under§3.3 hypotheses and X proper over algebraically closed k, every hyperplane section is geometrically connected, including those of excessive dimension.
computation: Every irreducible component of the proper incidence dominates the normal dual projective space. In its Stein factorization the finite generic fiber is geometrically connected, so its reduced algebra is one purely inseparable field extension; its degree need not be one. Every component of the finite Stein factor dominates the base, hence its reduction is integral. Over a normal affine base A, each element b of the finite reduced algebra has a p-power in Frac(A), and that power is integral, hence lies in A. Thus the reduced Stein factor is finite radicial and surjective, a universal homeomorphism. Nilpotents do not alter connectedness, and the Stein fibers are geometrically connected, so all original fibers are geometrically connected. In characteristic zero the purely inseparable extension is trivial. This is a present-run proof, retaining the source’s properness and component hypotheses.
fate: Established Zariski connectedness/Stein factorization specialization, in the exact dominant-component setting. The inserted properness is included in the modern statement.

statement: For a linear subsystem with base locus B, geometric irreducibility of the generic moving section follows from image dimension≥2 under projection, provided B contributes no divisorial component. status_on_pages: Proposition8.18 and subsequent reduction; several words and dimension labels damaged.
computation: For the blow-up of P² at p, pullbacks of all lines through p have fixed exceptional divisor; removing B gives an irreducible moving part but the whole divisor is reducible. The equality2 in the displayed geometric-irreducibility criterion must be a bound≥2.

statement: The nerve embeds small categories fully faithfully into simplicial sets. A local system is a functor taking every arrow to an isomorphism. Its category cohomology, computed by derived inverse limit with the chosen variance, agrees with cohomology of the nerve with that local system.
status_on_pages: Assertions credited to Quillen and Artin–Mazur; proof not given.
computation: An n-simplex is a composable n-tuple; a simplicial map is forced by objects and arrows and respects composition through2-simplices. The standard cosimplicial replacement gives the product cochain complex. Requiring only existing isomorphisms to be inverted is tautological and is not the local-system condition.
fate: Established classifying-space and category-cohomology theory. Thomason1980 recalls the homotopy comparison and Quillen Higher K-theory I gives the nerve formalism. The variance and local-system correction remain explicit.

statement: Internal categories in Cat are double categories, encoded by bisimplicial sets satisfying Segal conditions in each direction. Iteration gives n-fold categories and an action of the symmetric group permuting directions. Globularity is an additional discreteness constraint, not a consequence of Segal conditions alone.
fate: Established strict multiple-category/nerve theory. Modern terminology “bicategory” must not replace this manuscript’s double-category usage. The precise higher globularity convention must be stated before claiming an equivalence.

statement: Globular strict n-categories internal to abelian groups correspond to length-n chain complexes. Without globularity, n-fold internal categories instead give multicomplexes. After localization at the corresponding homology equivalences, mapping higher groupoids are governed by the appropriate truncation of derived Hom, requiring resolutions rather than the naive Hom complex.
status_on_pages: n=2 bicomplex reduction explained; general n and the RHom formulation proposed.
computation: In n=2 the discrete first row removes the off-axis terms, leaving a three-term chain complex; the double-complex identity becomes d²=0. Induction repeats this normalized-chain argument. statement: Symmetric monoidal categories admit homotopical group-completion constructions yielding connective K-theory spectra. computation: An ample twist makes bundles globally generated. A surjection from a finite free bundle onto a vector bundle splits locally, so its kernel is a vector bundle and −[F]=[K]−N. Exact polynomial identities are checked separately; affine global generation must not be assumed for every bundle.

statement: The converse claiming that equivalence of bounded locally constant derived categories over every fixed nonzero coefficient ring detects weak homotopy equivalence is false. Over Q it detects only rational cohomological information once the local systems are fixed.
status_on_pages: The converse is expressly asserted for an arbitrary nonzero ring.
computation: Let X=M(Z/p,n), n≥2, a finite simply connected Moore complex. Its reduced integral homology is Z/p in degree n, so it is not weakly contractible. Over Q its two-cell differential is multiplication by p, hence invertible. All Q-local systems are constant and their positive Ext groups are the rational cohomology of X with Hom coefficients, which vanishes. Bounded Postnikov induction therefore gives D^b_lc(X;Q)≃D^b(Q). Taking the face category of a finite triangulation gives the category-nerve formulation.
fate: Negative for the stated fixed arbitrary nonzero coefficient ring. Hatcher Example2.40 supplies the precise Moore-space construction; the derived-category deduction and rational cellular computation are independently checked here. The all-integral/all-coefficient formulation is a separate stronger criterion.

statement: For a locally split exact sequence 0→E′→E→E″→0 with E′ finite locally free of rank n, the chart of rank-n quotients restricting to an isomorphism on E′ is the sheaf of retractions E→E′. It is a torsor under Hom(E″,E′), identified with that additive sheaf only after a chosen splitting; when E″ is also finite locally free this is a vector bundle. The basis decompositions immediately preceding the sentence supply the splitting and finite-rank hypotheses. For an arbitrary exact sequence the retraction functor need not be locally nonempty.
status_on_pages: The chart proof says “canonically” after discussing chosen basis decompositions; the scope of “such an exact sequence” is ambiguous.
computation: A quotient in the chart can be identified with E′ and hence is a retraction. Differences of retractions factor uniquely through E″. Translating a chosen splitting by u in Hom(E″,E′) changes the origin, so there is no choice-free zero section. Local existence requires local splitting: 0→2Z→Z→Z/2→0 has no retraction near the prime2, even after a faithfully flat base change. The manuscript’s basis decompositions meet these requirements; the generalized exact-sequence wording needs them stated.
fate: The ordinary affine chart construction is established. The chosen-basis statement is valid; an extension to arbitrary exact sequences as a canonical vector-bundle identification requires the missing choice. This is the same qualification recorded in cote25, but the typed contexts are retained separately.

statement: Sending a small category C to its presheaf topos does not make all geometric morphisms arise from functors between the indexing categories. The source explicitly doubts full faithfulness; the distinction from the fully faithful nerve remains essential.
computation: Let D be the ordered set of all integers. The filtered-colimit functor Psh(D)→Set over D^op preserves all colimits and finite limits and has the constant-presheaf functor as right adjoint. It defines a point of Psh(D). It is not evaluation at any n: it sends every representable y(m) to a singleton, whereas evaluation at n sends y(n−1) to the empty set. A functor from the terminal category to D chooses n and induces evaluation, so this point proves non-fullness. This does not assert loss of every form of faithfulness.
fate: Established presheaf-topos point theory; SGA4IV Exercise7.6 distinguishes the representable/essential points, and the explicit nonrepresentable filtered-colimit point is independently proved here. Seminar and publication dates are kept separate.

statement: Subterminal objects are classified by the Sierpinski topos. This quotient of the object classifier is neither open nor closed; lattice complements must be taken in the full subtopos lattice.

computation.proof_or_check: A subterminal object is precisely an open of the base topos; a frame map from the three-element Sierpinski frame chooses exactly one such open. Sentences in the empty one-sort geometric theory have only false, inhabited and true truth conditions: existentially quantified equalities have a witness in any inhabited object. statement: For a commutative ring A, Spec(A) is zero-dimensional iff each f admits an idempotent decomposition A≃A_f×A/f^nA for some n, iff the principal ideals f^nA eventually stabilize. Compact here means Hausdorff compact, not merely quasi-compact.

computation.proof_or_check: If Spec(A) is zero-dimensional, D(f) is clopen and equals D(e) for an idempotent e; on eA, f is a unit, and on(1−e)A it is nilpotent. Conversely the decomposition forces every prime quotient to be a field. Stationary powers give f^n=f^{n+1}g and hence the same unit/nilpotent separation. Testing only artinian local rings is not established by this argument.

statement: Reduced commutative rings are models of the cartesian sequents x^n=0⇒x=0 (n≥1); their finitely presentable theory objects are reductions of finitely presented rings, and the classifier is the corresponding presheaf topos.

computation.proof_or_check: Reduced rings are a reflective full subcategory of rings with reflector A↦A_red and are closed under filtered colimits and all limits. The category is locally finitely presentable; maps from A_red to reduced B are maps A→B. Its finite colimits are reduced ring colimits. Power-map kernels in the source are subsets, not additive kernels; their union is the nilradical.
computation.limit: Analytic reasoning; no claim of machine formalization.

In a nonprincipal ultraproduct, x and y are nonnilpotent because every fixed power survives eventually, yet xy=0. Its nilradical is not prime. statement: Rings whose base is locally partitioned into prime-field algebra structures are classified by the presheaf category on finite-type affine schemes over the prime fields, with their empty affine objects identified. Components excluding the zero ring are disjoint; those allowing it meet in the common open Set point.

computation.proof_or_check: Different prime characteristics have only the zero ring in common. Open gluing of the pieces gives the topos and its point criterion: the glued topos has enough points iff each open piece does. This is local constancy of the prime-field choice in the base topos, not a claim that every ring has such a decomposition.

statement: In a topos, a domain with decidable zero embeds in its internal fraction field. A subring of a geometric field necessarily has decidable zero. Domain alone does not imply this constructive condition.

computation.proof_or_check: If zero is complemented, nonzero elements form a multiplicative subobject; localization at them is a field and the domain map is monic. Conversely a geometric field has complementary zero and units, whose pullback gives decidable zero in a subring. For the generic domain, a nonunit can vanish after quotient to a prime-domain residue, so the universally nonzero elements are only units.
computation.limit: Analytic reasoning; no claim of machine formalization.

fate: Caramello–Johnstone §1 gives the geometric field decomposition and distinguishes ordinary field models from their internal classifier. The internal fraction argument is reconstructed explicitly with its decidability hypothesis.

statement: If the evaluation M⊗Hom_A(M,A)→A is an isomorphism, M is finite locally free of rank1. Monogenicity holds locally, not necessarily globally.
status_on_pages: whole proof attempt canceled in the transcription

computation.proof_or_check: Write the inverse image of1 under evaluation as a finite sum of tensors m_i⊗phi_i; the values phi_i(m_i) generate the unit ideal. Locally where one is invertible, m_i is unimodular and M splits as A⊕N. The cross term N⊗A lies in the kernel of evaluation, so injectivity forces N=0. This finite open cover proves M finite locally free rank1. The ideal(2,1+sqrt(-5)) has I²=(2) and norm2, but a²+5b²=2 has no integer solution, so it is invertible and nonprincipal. Hom base change is used only after finite projectivity is established.
computation.limit: Executed exact finite or symbolic checks verify the named examples and identities only. The unrestricted claim depends on the separately recorded analytic proof and its hypotheses.

fate: Stacks0B8I proves precisely tensor inverse⇔finite locally free rank1 and identifies the inverse with Hom(M,A). The global-monogenic assertion is refuted by the stated ideal.

statement: For small C and regular κ, Ind_κ(C) is the free κ-filtered-colimit completion; its κ-presentables are the retract closure of C. An identification of a given E with that particular Ind_κ(C) requires the density and κ-filtered comma presentation. Accessible functors admit such a description at suitable ranks.

computation.proof_or_check: An object presented by a κ-filtered colimit is κ-presentable only if its identity factors through a stage, hence is a retract. Conversely retracts of representables remain presentable. The canonical comma presentation is κ-filtered in the valid Ind setting. Density alone does not imply Ind of the selected C: {1} is dense in Set but its Ind category is terminal. This does not refute Set’s accessibility with a larger small presentable subcategory.
computation.limit: Analytic reasoning; no claim of machine formalization.

statement: For a doctrine prescribing specified limits and colimits, a J-limit of models is pointwise when it exists in the target and commutes there with the prescribed colimits; limits commute with the prescribed limits. Change of target preserves this construction when the target functor preserves the J-limit. The dual statement exchanges limits and colimits.

statement: A no-operation small presentation represents a small category. Inverting all arrows gives its groupoid completion; identifying parallel arrows gives its reachability preorder; further identifying mutually comparable objects gives its poset reflection.

computation.proof_or_check: Formal words of arrows and inverses, modulo compositions and inverse relations, have the groupoid universal property. The preorder has one arrow exactly when a path exists. Its antisymmetrization identifies x and y when paths exist both ways. A preorder need not already be a poset, so those last two constructions must remain distinct.

statement: A Grothendieck topos has a conservative family of essential points iff it is equivalent to a presheaf topos. Essential points correspond to nonempty connected projectives; for PSh(C) their category is the Karoubi completion of C. An essential geometric morphism is characterized by its inverse image preserving all small limits, equivalently products.

statement: There are nondegenerate Grothendieck topoi with no Set-valued points. Thus absence of Set models does not mean that the geometric theory is inconsistent in all topoi.

computation.proof_or_check: Let B be a complete atomless Boolean algebra, for example regular opens of R. A frame map B→2 preserves complements and arbitrary joins, hence arbitrary meets. The meet of its1-fiber would be a nonzero atom, impossible. Therefore Sh(B) has no points, while0≠1 in its subterminal frame proves nondegeneracy. The associated propositional geometric theory has B-valued models despite no Set model.
computation.limit: Analytic reasoning; no claim of machine formalization.

computation.proof_or_check: There are countably many finite presentations over Z and countably many maps between any two such rings, so choose a countable skeleton of the finite-type affine site; it has finite limits. The D_n family over the generic element is countable, and its pullbacks along the countably many site arrows generate a countable coverage. Makkai–Reyes6.2.4 therefore supplies enough points. No finite subfamily covers: for maximal exponent N, the element t in F_2[t]/(t^(N+1)) has neither a unit component nor t^n=0 for n≤N. This is a general nilpotence-order argument, not a finite-sample inference.
computation.limit: Analytic reasoning; no claim of machine formalization.

fate: Makkai–Reyes, First Order Categorical Logic (1977), Theorem6.2.4, proves enough points for separable topoi. The opened 2018 corrected retyping states the countable-category/countable-basic-cover hypothesis and gives the proof on printed p125. The original book metadata and retyping provenance were separately opened; no earlier circulation date is asserted.

statement: For an irreducible finite-type k-scheme X and any k-morphism X→P^r, its section over the generic point of the dual space is empty or irreducible; if nonempty it dominates X. This is ordinary, not geometric, irreducibility.
computation: Proof: the total incidence over X is irreducible. Localizing its coordinate rings at the nonzero functions of the dual base gives an empty scheme or an irreducible generic fiber, whose generic point is also generic in the incidence and hence maps to the generic point of X.
fate: The incidence projective-bundle argument proves this exact statement. Stacks0G4C separately treats the stronger geometric version, whose image-dimension hypothesis must not be omitted.

statement: The image in P^r of the generic hyperplane consists exactly of the nonclosed points. For constructible Z⊂X of finite type over k, its generic section is empty iff f(Z) is finite.
computation: Proof: a closed point has finite residue extension, so its incidence image is a proper hyperplane locus. The closure of a nonclosed point has positive dimension; if a hyperplane missed it, that closure would be both affine and proper, hence finite. A constructible subset of a finite-type Jacobson space consisting only of closed points is finite.
fate: The exact visibility statement follows from projective incidence and the fact that a positive-dimensional projective closed subset meets every hyperplane. Stacks0G4C uses the same generic-section setup.

statement: Under the component-image and finite-image-deletion hypotheses of3.3, with X proper over an algebraically closed field, every hyperplane section is connected, including excess-dimensional sections.
computation: Proof: for an integral component apply Stein factorization to proper incidence. Its generic fiber is geometrically connected. The reduced finite factor is generically purely inseparable over the normal projective dual space; on a normal affine base each integral element has a p-power in the base, so this finite factor is universally injective and has connected fibers (birational in characteristic0). For reducible X, form the finite graph of components joined when their intersection has positive-dimensional image. The deletion hypothesis makes this graph connected. Such an intersection has proper positive-dimensional image, which meets every hyperplane. Each component section is connected, so their union is connected.
fate: For an integral source, EGA III1 Corollary4.3.7 and Remark4.3.8, printed133, gives the proper connectedness-specialization step over the normal dual projective space. Martinelli–Naranjo–Pirola Theorem1.1 supplies the irreducible projective case in any characteristic. The manuscript’s reducible case additionally uses its finite-image-deletion hypothesis; it is not a verbatim case of either cited theorem.

statement: For smooth geometrically irreducible immersed X⊂P^r with nonempty conormal incidence, generic unramifiedness of the conormal projection is equivalent to a finite separable function-field extension and to a nonsupersingular tangency. Under these hypotheses the dual is a hypersurface and the conormal map is birational; over the smooth dual it is an open immersion, and an isomorphism if X is proper.
computation: Targeted proof check: the differential image at (x,H) identifies the hyperplane in the dual tangent space determined by x; two points over a smooth dual point must therefore coincide. Properness upgrades the open immersion to an isomorphism there.
fate: The exact separable-duality argument is developed in SGA7II XVII§3. Nonempty incidence and immersion are essential; neither a linear full-dimensional X nor arbitrary unramified multiple covers can be silently included in the birational statement.

statement: The chart of rank-n quotients restricting to an isomorphism on E′ is identified canonically with the vector bundle after a basis decomposition of E. The text deletes “sommes directes” in favor of exact sequences but retains the preceding basis choice. Extending “canonical” to an arbitrary exact sequence is a stronger reading, not forced by that context.
computation: Proof: two retractions E→E′ differ by a map E″→E′, and retractions exist locally for a locally split sequence. A global retraction is equivalent to a splitting. A nonzero extension of O by O on a genus1 curve is locally split and has finite locally free terms, but no global retraction because its class in Ext¹(O,O)=H¹(O) is nonzero. Its retraction torsor therefore has no global zero section. This refutes only the unrestricted canonical-trivialization reading. The sequence0→2Z→Z→Z/2→0 has no retraction even after faithfully flat base change, illustrating the necessity of local splitting for the torsor formulation.
fate: The chosen-basis chart is valid. For a locally split exact sequence with finite locally free E′ and E″, the chart is the torsor of retractions under Hom(E″,E′); choosing a splitting trivializes it. A nonsplit extension shows that a choice-free global vector-bundle identification is false. Without local splitting even the torsor assertion can fail. Stacks089R uses the valid split coordinate charts. The unresolved issue is the scope of the source’s “une telle suite exacte,” not the standard chart theorem.

statement: For a complex poly-elementary neighborhood of dimension n, the analytic space is a K(pi,1); its fundamental group is built by successive extensions by finitely generated free groups, and its universal cover is homeomorphic toC^n. This is a topological, not biholomorphic, assertion.
computation: Proof: compactify each curve fibration with finite étale boundary. Ehresmann’s theorem for the compact pair gives a locally trivial bundle of punctured surfaces. Pull to the universal cover of the base; the bundle over its contractible R^(2n−2) base is trivial, and then take the contractible surface cover R². The homotopy exact sequence gives the free-group extension and vanishing higher homotopy.
fate: SGA4III XI’s comparison argument uses elementary neighborhoods and their topological fibration structure. A punctured compact complex curve has contractible universal cover; the tower gives asphericity. The stronger homeomorphism statement uses triviality of a smooth bundle over a contractible base, not uniformization in several variables.

statement: For E finite locally free of rank at least2 everywhere, the relative effective degree-n divisors in P(E), n≥0, are represented by P((Sym^n E)^vee). Scan107 expressly corrects scan5, which used Sym^n(E^vee). A divisor is a fiberwise regular section of p*M(n), equivalently a sub-line-bundle M^−1 of Sym^n E. The separate cancelled restatement on scan112 omits the dual on Sym^n E and does not repeat the rank-at-least2 hypothesis; it is retained as another source occurrence, not silently normalized. The formula is not extended to rank1: then P(E)=S, the relative Cartier divisor is empty, and the degree labels do not distinguish different divisors.
computation: Proof: every nonzero homogeneous polynomial over a field is a nonzerodivisor in its polynomial ring. Fiberwise nonzero sections therefore give relative Cartier divisors. A locally split line inclusion in Sym^n E dualizes to a rank-one quotient of (Sym^n E)^vee, exactly the functor represented by the stated projective bundle.
fate: The relative Cartier criterion and universal quotient property establish the corrected formula. Over arbitrary characteristic, dual of Sym^n E must not be replaced canonically by Sym^n(E^vee); divided-power issues make the distinction real. Degree0 parametrizes the empty divisor.

statement: Let f:X→S be proper, flat and finitely presented, with universally f*O_X=O_S, and L invertible. If a finitely presented Q corepresents G↦f*(L tensor f*G), the divisors with associated bundle L up to a base twist form a retrocompact open in P(Q). For geometrically integral fibers this is all of P(Q).
computation: Proof: a quotient Q→M corresponds to a section of L tensor f*M. The locus where its restriction to every fiber is regular is open by the flat finite-presentation Cartier criterion; properness of X/S gives the required relative open condition in the parameter. On geometrically integral fibers every nonzero section of an invertible sheaf is regular.

The universal f*O condition is needed for the scalar quotient and uniqueness, and geometric integrality is needed for every nonzero section to be regular. statement: For D⊂X×_S T a relative Cartier family, its fixed-point locus Z consists of x such that the whole fiber T_x lies set-theoretically in D_x. Under universal openness of T/S, Z is closed. If T/S is flat, locally finitely presented with geometrically irreducible S1 fibers, D transposes to a relative Cartier family over X exactly away from Z. With T proper, the analogous associated-point obstruction Z′ is closed.
computation: Proof: X−Z is the image of (X×T)−D under the open projection, hence open. An irreducible noetherian S1 geometric fiber has its unique generic point as its only associated point. A local equation is regular exactly when it avoids that prime, equivalently when it is not nilpotent; mere nonzero is insufficient on a nonreduced fiber. The relative Cartier locus W in X×T is open under the stated finite-presentation and flatness hypotheses. For proper T/S, the image of its closed complement under X×T→X is closed, giving Z′.
fate: The openness and fiberwise Cartier arguments are standard consequences of the relative Cartier criterion. The S1 and geometric irreducibility assumptions cannot be replaced by topological irreducibility alone; regularity is tested at all associated points. The source explicitly distinguishes Z from Z′ in the general case.

statement: A basepoint-free linear system on X/S with projective parameter P corresponds to a morphism to the dual projective bundle whose image on every geometric associated component spans that bundle. This componentwise condition ensures every member is a relative Cartier divisor.
computation: Proof: a section of an invertible sheaf is regular iff it avoids all associated points. A nonzero parameter hyperplane pulls back to zero at an associated generic point precisely when it contains the corresponding component image. Applying this on every geometric fiber gives the assertion.
fate: The universal quotient construction proves the map correspondence; the componentwise spanning condition is exactly nonvanishing at all associated points. The weaker condition that the union of all components spans does not suffice, since a hyperplane may contain one component.

statement: Let X→S be locally of finite presentation, F a quasi-coherent finitely presented S-flat module, T⊂X closed, and j:X−T→X a quasi-compact open immersion. Fiberwise depth of F at every point of T at least1 gives F→j*F|U injective; depth at least2 gives an isomorphism. In the line-bundle application X/S is flat with fiberwise depth of O_X at least2 on T: then a bundle L on U extends invertibly exactly when j*L is invertible, uniquely with its comparison.
computation: Proof: locally a finitely generated ideal defines T because j is quasi-compact. The fiber-depth hypothesis supplies a length1 or2 regular sequence in that ideal after localization; EGA IV3 11.3.8 lifts its regularity for the base-flat module. The local-cohomology sequence0→H^0_T(F)→F→j*F|U→H^1_T(F)→0 then gives injectivity or bijectivity. In the noetherian case this is exactly IV2 5.10.2/5.10.5. Apply the depth2 statement to Hom bundles for uniqueness of invertible extensions; if j*L is invertible it supplies existence.
fate: EGA IV2 5.10.2 and5.10.5, printed114–116, proves the depth1/2 Hartogs criteria over locally noetherian schemes;6.3.1, printed138–139, compares flat-module depth with fiber depth. EGA IV3 11.3.7–8, printed135–136, supplies the finite-presentation relative regular-sequence mechanism used to remove noetherian hypotheses. The rational-map application still requires componentwise nondegeneracy.

statement: In the locally factorial setting, a divisor on an open whose complement has codimension at least2 extends uniquely as a Cartier divisor; the associated line bundle extension gives the corresponding rational-map/linear-system extension when the stated nondegeneracy remains true.
computation: Proof: on a locally factorial noetherian scheme a codimension1 cycle defines a Cartier divisor. Closure of the codimension1 components from U gives the unique Weil divisor on X because the complement contributes none. Local factoriality makes this closure Cartier.
fate: The regular-local factoriality theorem and the Cartier–Weil correspondence are classical ingredients. The source does not prove an unrestricted extension across codimension1, and the earlier fixed-divisor ambiguity must not be reintroduced.

statement: For proper flat geometrically integral fibers and a cohomology corepresentative Q, linear systems with fixed parameter rank correspond to locally free quotients Q→E^vee, modulo parameter isomorphism, hence to a Grassmannian. A system is complete exactly when its fiber spaces equal all H^0(X_s,L_s).
computation: Proof: adjunction identifies a section map E→f*L with a map Q→E^vee; fiberwise injectivity of the former is fiberwise surjectivity of the latter. Nakayama gives a locally free quotient. Completeness means this quotient has full fiber dimension and the cohomology base-change comparison is an isomorphism.
fate: EGA III2 Th7.7.6 supplies Q; the Grassmannian quotient functor gives the moduli statement. Completeness is preserved by base change when stated geometrically with the required cohomology/base-change isomorphisms. A marginal apparent negation in scan126 conflicts with that formulation and is flagged without alteration.

statement: The projective-frame lemma requires each specified component image to span the projective parameter space. Under that hypothesis an automorphism fixing the images is scalar on the associated vector space; merely spanning by the union of components is insufficient.
computation: Proof: n+2 points in projective general position form a projective frame; fixing the first n+1 diagonalizes a representing matrix, and fixing their sum makes all diagonal entries equal. A union of coordinate points spans but admits a diagonal torus of automorphisms, so the weakened union formulation fails.
fate: This is the classical projective-frame argument. It supports the revised automorphism-faithfulness proof, with scheme-valued infinitesimal verification still needed for a monomorphism of functors.

statement: For an effective Cartier D⊂X the tangent space to Div at D is H^0(D,N_D/X); the tangent space to Hom(X,P) at f is Hom(f*Ω_P,O_X). The proof of functorial faithfulness needs Artin-local/infinitesimal control, not only injectivity on geometric points.
computation: Proof: deform an ideal locally generated by t to(t+εa); changing the generator identifies a modulo(t), giving Hom(I/I²,O_D)=N_D/X. A map deformation is a derivation f^*O_P→O_X, equivalently Hom(f*Ω_P,O_X). These are first-order statements only; induction along square-zero extensions is required for the stated stronger functor conclusion.
fate: Grothendieck’s published Bourbaki Exposé221 (May1961),5.3–5.5, printed270–271, explicitly gives the Hilbert tangent and Cartier-divisor formulas. The square-zero calculation also proves the Hom formula. The text’s O_P in that formula is a type error. Its references to future §§25–26 do not establish the general arbitrary-functor monomorphism criterion, which remains a separate incomplete step; the1961 tangent result is already known when this draft is written.

statement: Uniqueness of the parameter identification permits fppf descent of a linear system, but the descended parameter need only be a Brauer–Severi variety. Scan137 proposes treating projective bundles and their twisted forms using PGL torsors.

statement: On the singular-zero scheme of a line-bundle section, the second principal part is a canonical quadratic form in the relative cotangent module, with the line-bundle twist. Its polar determinant defines a closed nonsupersingularity obstruction compatible with arbitrary base change.
computation: Proof: changing local coordinates changes the quadratic term by the symmetric-square cotangent change when the constant and linear terms vanish. Determinants transform by the square determinant character and the appropriate line-bundle power, so they glue and commute with base change.
fate: The modern quadratic-form treatment in Conrad2014 AppendixC and SGA7II XII gives the determinant construction. This polar determinant detects nonsupersingularity; in odd rank characteristic2 it does not detect ordinary smoothness, which instead uses the half-discriminant.

statement: The proof identifies smoothness of a closed subscheme with injectivity of its conormal map as a sheaf, without specifying fiberwise injectivity or a locally split injection.
computation: Proof: in B=k[x,y]/(xy), the conormal map B→B² sends1 to(y,x). Its kernel is ann(x)∩ann(y)=(y)∩(x)=0, so it is sheaf-injective. At the origin its fiber map is zero, and Spec(B) is a singular node.
fate: For an lci immersion into a smooth scheme the smoothness criterion is injectivity after passage to the residue field, equivalently local splitting with locally free cokernel. A merely injective sheaf map allows singular hypersurfaces.

statement: The isolated nonsupersingular hypersurface claim is correct under regular-local ambient assumptions, but the early normality threshold uses the ambient dimension as if it were the hypersurface dimension. In a regular-local presentation one removes m−1 independent linear equations, leaving a hypersurface whose quadratic initial form is smooth.

statement: A homogeneous polynomial whose image is nonzero on every residue-field fiber gives injective multiplication in each degree between finite locally free symmetric powers, with locally free cokernel. The resulting graded pieces are flat and have the expected ranks. Regular complete-intersection zeros in the stated smooth relative setting are flat over the base.
computation: Proof: over a residue field multiplication by a nonzero polynomial is injective. A map between finite free modules which is fiberwise injective is locally a split injection, by choosing a nonvanishing maximal minor; the cokernel is locally free. statement: Scan154 identifies an invertible direct-summand kernel with a fiber-rank condition; scan166 expressly corrects that earlier equivalence on page15 line10. The separate constant-rank lemma on scan155 already assumes that the exterior-power map vanishes as a morphism, not merely at residue-field points, and is valid with its remaining rank hypothesis. computation: Proof: multiplication by ε on A=k[ε]/(ε²) is zero on its unique residue field but is not the zero map. In contrast, if a rank-r minor is a unit, row/column reduction puts a matrix in block form diag(I_r,B); vanishing of all(r+1)-minors forces B=0 as a matrix over A.

statement: A degree-e form on a finite locally free module is smooth if it is nonzero on every fiber and its projective zero scheme is smooth over the base. This is detected after arbitrary surjective base change and defines an open locus. The Jacobian criterion uses the ideal generated by the form and all partial derivatives.

Fiberwise smoothness plus the fiberwise nonzero Cartier condition gives smoothness. On an affine chart the Jacobian ideal is generated by f and its derivatives; homogeneous compatibility gives the irrelevant-ideal power criterion.
fate: The smoothness criterion and properness of projective space give openness. Euler’s formula permits dropping the form only when e is invertible; retaining it makes the statement valid in every characteristic. After K=k(t) base change, the K-rational point t=t0 has local tangent cone K[x,y,w]/(xy), where w=t−t0. Its projective quadric is singular at[0:0:1], and the singular locus is not isolated. Thus geometric ordinaryness at that rational point fails.
fate: Closed finite separable residue extensions do not introduce extra tangent directions, so the standard comparison holds. At a nonclosed point, base change to its residue field followed by the rational geometric point changes the local embedding dimension; the proposed strengthening fails.

statement: For a positive-rank locally free module, a quadratic form is smooth when it is fiberwise nonzero and its projective quadric is smooth. A nondegenerate polar form implies smoothness; the converse holds in even rank or when2 is invertible. In odd rank characteristic2, smoothness instead means polar radical dimension1 and nonzero quadratic restriction to that line.
computation: Proof: over a field a projective singular point is a nonzero vector v with B(v,−)=0 and Q(v)=0. If2 is invertible, B(v,v)=2Q(v) makes any radical vector singular. In characteristic2, an alternating polar matrix has even rank; smoothness permits exactly a one-dimensional radical on which Q is nonzero. These fiber criteria give the statement over a base.

statement: For odd rank, the determinant of the universal polar matrix is divisible over Z by2 with content exactly2. Proof: modulo2 an odd alternating matrix has determinant0, so every universal coefficient is even. On the standard odd form the determinant is±2, so the content is exactly2. statement: Smooth rank-n quadratic forms are equivalent to fppf torsors under the standard orthogonal group O_n. The equivalence sends a form to its isomorphism torsor and a torsor to the descended standard vector bundle and quadratic form.

statement: The draft asserts étale local triviality in the smooth-orthogonal cases and a Zariski-local finite étale strengthening via SGA3 XXIV; in odd rank it proposes first a finite locally free μ2 cover and then the smooth-group theorem. It supplies the rank-one characteristic2 example obstructing étale trivialization. These paragraphs assert cover results; the nearby priority and terminology question concerns the corrected discriminant and is separately recorded as C-SA23-hyp-106.
computation: Targeted proof check: original and corrected SGA3 XXIV4.1.1 and4.2.3 were read, including the split-torus/Pic(semilocal)=0 argument. The orthogonal component quotient is finite étale in even rank and when2 is invertible; the connected split SO factor is reductive. In odd rank O=μ2×SO′, so first take the finite locally free μ2 torsor and then the finite étale SO′ cover of the resulting semilocal ring. For a∈k* nonsquare in characteristic2, an isometry aT²≅T² needs a purely inseparable square root, which no separable extension contains; k[t]/(t²−a) is nevertheless a finite faithfully flat cover.
fate: SGA3 XXIV4.2.3 proves that a torsor under a split reductive group over a semilocal base is trivialized by a finite étale surjective cover. Apply this to the split special orthogonal factor after the finite component torsor; in odd rank first use the finite locally free μ2 torsor. Finite presentation spreads the resulting cover and isometry from a local base to a Zariski neighborhood. Thus the asserted Zariski-local finite étale trivialization in the smooth cases, and finite flat trivialization in general, are established. This is not a theorem about arbitrary smooth groups.

statement: The author asks whether, after a degree-n Veronese with n≥2, the dual discriminant can no longer contain the family of all hyperplanes through a fixed positive-dimensional linear subspace C. No transversality or first-jet hypothesis on C is written. The unrestricted hope is false even for the degree2 embedding of a smooth projective plane in characteristic0.
computation: computations.py veronese_fixed_linear_space verifies q(p)=0 and all three partial derivatives vanish at p=[0:0:1] for q=a x²+b y². Proof: take k algebraically closed of characteristic0, f=id on P², and its degree2 Veronese v₂:P²→P⁵. The independent coordinate equations U_x²=U_y²=0 define C≅P³. Every hyperplane containing C pulls back to a nonzero member of that pencil, which is singular at p. The intersection C∩v₂(P²) has local ideal(x²,y²), so it is even finite, although nonreduced. For every degree n≥2 the analogous pencil a x^n+b y^n lies in the square of the maximal ideal at p and gives the same obstruction. All smoothness, irreducibility, projectivity and unramifiedness assumptions on X and f hold.

Stacks33.47.1 and33.47.3 distinguish smoothness away from a fixed base subscheme from the first-jet obstruction at its points. statement: For a flat, locally finitely presented projective morphism X→S, the source promises a later proof that the functor of relative effective Cartier divisors on X is representable. statement: A space is noetherian if every closed subset has finitely many irreducible components and descending chains of irreducible closed subsets stabilize. In particular a locally finite family of irreducible components controls connected components by finite incidence.
computation: A descending chain of closed sets produces a finitely branching tree of proper irreducible descendants; an infinite strict chain gives an infinite branch, contradicting the irreducible-chain hypothesis. The converse is immediate. Quasi-compactness stated separately is redundant under the full criterion.

statement: Restriction of an affine equation functor to field-valued points determines only the radical of its ideal. Nil(A) is the intersection of all prime ideals, equivalently kernels of maps to fields. Functions on V_A are morphisms to A¹ and recover A only when the full functor is retained.
computation: k[ε]/(ε²) and k have the same field-valued points, but evaluating the full functor on dual numbers distinguishes them. For finite-type algebras over algebraically closed fields, rational-point tests use the Nullstellensatz. Over a general base, finite extensions of all prime residue fields also suffice: pass to a fiber and choose a closed point after localizing at the element to detect.
fate: Classical Nullstellensatz and nilradical results. The general-base statement is valid when residue fields means all prime residue fields; restricting only to closed residue points would require a Jacobson-type qualification.

statement: Colimits in affine schemes are opposite limits of rings, but can differ from sheaf or scheme quotients. For GL_n and its upper-triangular subgroup, the flag-variety quotient has only constant global functions over a field, so its affine quotient is Spec k.
status_on_pages: Warning and example; finite-relation quotient topic deferred.
computation: The flag variety is proper geometrically connected with Γ(O)=k; invariant regular functions on GL_n descend along its torsor to the flag variety and are constant. Finite relations require exact effectiveness hypotheses and cannot be certified from “OK” alone. Published Raicu example is used as a counterexample to effectivity; its computer algebra certificate was not rerun here and is labelled background evidence, not a new computation.
fate: The affine versus geometric quotient warning is established (Stacks Groupoids example-quotient-projective-line). Finite locally free equivalence relations are effective: Stacks39.23.9 tag03BM. Mere finiteness does not imply effectivity: Raicu appendix§50 in Kollar2011 pp252–254 gives finite scheme-theoretic relations on A² strictly smaller than the quotient fiber product. Kollar Theorem6 proves geometric quotient existence for finite set-theoretic relations on algebraic spaces essentially of finite type over Noetherian F_p-schemes. Witaszek2022 Theorem1.4 extends existence over excellent bases for separated finite-type algebraic spaces provided the characteristic-zero quotient already exists separated finite type. The manuscript does not specify which notion its “OK” intends. The general characteristic-zero scheme-theoretic existence question is Question8 in Kollar2011; this search did not locate a resolution as of19Nov2026, which is not a certification that it remains open.
